summary.headline: NCC Q2 FY27 consol turnover rose 32% to INR6,042 crore, with FY27 guidance of 8-10% growth retained.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 turnover grew 32% YoY to INR6,042 crore, the highest-ever Q2 revenue on a consol basis, and H1 turnover rose 21% to INR11,884 crore. Consol EBITDA margin was 8.79% in Q2 (8.66% a year earlier) and 9.1% for H1. Order book stood at INR80,167 crore at 30 September, up 11% YoY, with INR4,838 crore booked in the quarter and INR2,381 crore more in October. Management retained FY27 guidance (revenue growth 8-10%, EBITDA margin 8.5-9%, order inflow INR22,000-25,000 crore) but did not explain why H2 growth would slow, which drew sustained analyst questioning. Working capital eased, receivable days fell to 53 and JJM outstandings declined, while consolidated net debt rose to INR3,887 crore.

segments.name: Order book by division
segments.commentary: Buildings INR22,367 crore (28%), Transportation INR15,682 crore (20%), Electrical T&D INR12,370 crore (15%), Mining INR12,400 crore (15%), Water and Railway INR12,126 crore (15%), Irrigation and others INR5,220 crore (7%). Standalone order book INR71,293 crore; subsidiaries INR8,874 crore (mining 5,923, transportation 2,431, smart meters 520).

segments.name: Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM)
segments.commentary: Outstanding receivable INR2,246 crore including all states, with trade receivables at INR344 crore and unbilled at INR2,009 crore. JJM backlog excluding O&M is INR5,412-5,413 crore; the UP legacy backlog is expected to be substantially complete by March 2027. H1 JJM receipts were about INR1,720 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance retained: revenue growth 8-10%, EBITDA margin 8.5-9%, order inflow INR22,000-25,000 crore.
Order inflow so far (including October) is INR11,108 crore, about 50% of the lower band of guidance.
FY27 capex to be about INR500 crore; INR253 crore spent in H1, so about INR250 crore in H2. FY28 capex expected to be similar, driven by the Amrapali mining project in Jharkhand.

Finance cost expected to hold at about INR166 crore per quarter; depreciation to rise in Q3 and Q4 as the TBM is in use from September 2026 and mining capex comes on stream, with depreciation at about 1.48% of revenue.
Vizag land sale receivable of INR270 crore expected to be fully recovered by end of Q4 FY27.
Retention of Ken-Betwa contract value is about INR3,389 crore per NCC's share, with unbilled revenue to be recognised as work progresses.
capex_capacity: Q2 FY27 capex INR83 crore; H1 capex INR253 crore against FY27 budget of about INR500 crore, excluding TBM which was capitalised from September 2026.
TBM capitalised and put to use in September 2026; mining project in Jharkhand (Amrapali) is capital intensive.
Smart meter projects are HAM-accounted; other financial liabilities of INR8,163 crore on the consol balance sheet relate to smart meter receivables, per management.
BharatNet work about 11% executed across MP and Uttarakhand, with about INR1,000 crore spent; housed under Electricals and T&D.
Smart meter installation about 51% complete, 49% outstanding.
demand_pricing: Management said 81% of contracts have escalation clauses, so raw material price increases are largely offset through price variation.
Govt client payment cycles are 50-60 days from certification; payment cycle broadly improving, including from JJM.
AP Capital City order book INR14,500 crore; receivables there realised within 30-40 days, per management.
Bid pipeline unchanged at about INR2.5 lakh crore as shared in May; no segment-wise breakup given.
Retention money at INR2,547 crore (up about INR150 crore QoQ); contract retention 5%, up to 20% in some electrical contracts; can be partly replaced by bank guarantee.

qa_highlights.question: Why retain 8-10% FY27 growth after 21% H1 growth, implying a sharp H2 slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is for the full year, H1 was strong on mining and other projects, and Q3 is too early to comment; guidance was retained.

qa_highlights.question: Why is retention money high relative to revenue, and can it be released?
qa_highlights.answer: Newer contracts carry 5% retention, some electrical contracts up to 20%, and CC road contracts in Mumbai high; retention will persist, with partial bank guarantee substitution possible on some contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Is the JJM payment improvement sustainable, and what is the outstanding?
qa_highlights.answer: JJM outstanding is INR2,246 crore; INR1,720 crore received in H1; JJM backlog excluding O&M is about INR5,412 crore, with UP legacy work largely done by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the unbilled revenue level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shift to EPC milestone billing and BharatNet and AP Capital City work drive unbilled; it is expected to remain at a similar level and to be realised progressively.

qa_highlights.question: Is the guidance for order inflow achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Inflow of INR11,108 crore including October is about 50% of the lower band; management retained the INR22,000-25,000 crore guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Hyderabad investment of INR107-108 crore under construction?
qa_highlights.answer: It is an investment in a stalled Hyderabad project under NCLT and RERA proceedings; management said it is fully secured and not at risk of non-recovery, though timing is uncertain.

risks_watch: Guidance implies a sharp H2 slowdown: 8-10% full-year growth against 21% in H1 means H2 growth may be low or negative.
Consol net debt rose to INR3,887 crore (from INR3,513 crore at Q1); standalone debt INR2,471 crore; debt-equity 0.32.
Retention money rising (INR2,547 crore, about 13% of revenue), tying up working capital.
Depreciation and finance cost trajectory as the TBM and mining projects enter service.
Mobilisation advances fell to INR2,925 crore; interest-bearing share fell from 60% to 53% at 9.07%.
Unresolved matters: Hyderabad investment stuck in NCLT, and the Ken-Betwa share and smart meter liability split were not provided on the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating performance and receivables, but evasive on guidance: management repeatedly declined to explain why H2 growth would slow, citing that the Q3 is still open. Some answers were deferred offline, such as Ken-Betwa share and smart meter liability split.
key_quotes: We have decided to retain our guidance for FY27.
The order book of INR80,167 crores is consisting of order book of INR71,293 crores at standalone level and INR8,874 crores of the subsidiaries.
There is no sticky unbilled revenue. The unbilled revenue is progressively realizing.
Definitely, the amount of investment is completely secured. There is no problem in recoverability of this investment.

adds.what: Tunnel boring machine (TBM) capitalised and put to use
Amrapali mining project in Jharkhand (capital-intensive, comes on stream in later periods)

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 8-10% (midpoint 9%) is retained, but management did not explain why H2 growth would slow after Q2's 32% and H1's 21%; support is an order book of INR80,167 crore (up 11%) plus a TBM now in use, while order inflow of INR11,108 crore is only about 50% of the lower band of the INR22,000-25,000 crore guidance.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consol EBITDA margin 8.79% in Q2 vs 8.66% YoY and 9.1% for H1, within FY27 guidance of 8.5-9%, with 81% of contracts carrying escalation clauses offsetting raw material moves, but depreciation rising to about 1.48% of revenue in Q3-Q4 weighs on profit.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: TBM capitalised and in use from September 2026, and the Amrapali mining project in Jharkhand is capital-intensive and comes on stream in later periods, with FY27 capex of about INR500 crore (INR253 crore spent in H1) and FY28 capex similar.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book of INR80,167 crore (up 11% YoY) and Q2 consol turnover up 32% to INR6,042 crore support volumes, but guidance implies a sharp H2 slowdown and order inflow of INR11,108 crore is about 50% of the lower band.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed, so there is no utilisation-based trigger, and management only signalled FY28 capex similar to FY27 (about INR500 crore) driven by Amrapali mining, which is already committed rather than a new announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance of 8-10% revenue growth was retained, and order inflow of INR11,108 crore is only about 50% of the lower band of INR22,000-25,000 crore, so there is no basis for a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue grew 21% against full-year guidance of 8-10%, implying H2 growth near zero or negative, yet management declined to explain the slowdown and order inflow is about 50% of the lower band, so a cut is a real risk.

rows.label: Receivable days fall and JJM outstanding declines
rows.why: Trade receivables fell to INR2,697 crore (53 days) from INR3,055 crore (68 days) in Q1, and JJM outstanding is INR2,246 crore with INR1,720 crore received in H1, though retention money at INR2,547 crore keeps working capital at 96 days.

rows.label: Order inflow to reach guidance
rows.why: Inflow of INR11,108 crore including October is about 50% of the lower band of INR22,000-25,000 crore, with half the year gone, so the guidance looks hard to meet.

rows.label: Consol net debt rising
rows.why: Consol net debt rose to INR3,887 crore from INR3,513 crore at Q1 and INR2,643 crore a year earlier, with finance cost steady at about INR166 crore a quarter, so debt reduction is not signalled.

tone.note: Management was confident on operating performance and receivables but evasive on why H2 growth would slow under retained 8-10% guidance; analysts pressed on the H2 slowdown, order inflow at about 50% of the lower band, and the Ken-Betwa and smart meter liability splits, which were deferred offline.
